items.text: As we recover from the COVID-19 pandemic, we must remember the devastating effects of another public health crisis: HIV/AIDS. On this day in 1990, the Ryan White CARE Act was enacted, providing hope for those in need of lifesaving care and treatment.

The legislation is named for Indiana’s Ryan White, whose family fiercely advocated for a federal response. To this day, the Ryan White CARE Act is the largest US program dedicated to research, awareness, and treatment of HIV/AIDS.

On Labor Day, we express our thanks to the workers who make our country what it is. But we also must remember the rights they are owed: fair treatment, respect, and equal opportunity to succeed. https://t.co/6CwAQAuTQn

Hard working rail workers shouldn’t have to face the risk of a strike to be treated fairly or exercise workplace rights. The railroad industry is essential to our state and national economies, including the rail yards in Indianapolis & the maintenance facilities in Beech Grove.

Each year, we acknowledge #WorldAIDSDay to remember the lives lost and renew our vow to fight this disease. We have the tools to prevent AIDS-related deaths. We must encourage testing, promote education, and end stigmas that prevent people from receiving life-saving treatment. https://t.co/1hAznYP4Cc

Today, I am proud to celebrate 20 years of success of the George McGovern-Robert Dole International Food for Education and Child Nutrition Program. The program has made an impact on the lives of 31 million children and families in 48 countries.
Today is Rare Disease Day, a time to advance the development of safe, effective treatment options to address the unmet needs of patients with rare diseases – many of whom are children.

For 58 years, @HeadStartgov has supported children’s success in school and in life. Today, Head Start serves over 13,400 Hoosier families in health, nutrition, and education services.
 
As a proud Head Start alum, I’ll keep fighting for every child to reach their full potential.

Moms often face bias, career interruptions, & lower pay after having a child – leading to moms making 62 cents for every dollar dads make. 

On #MomsEqualPayDay, we must acknowledge the unequal treatment of moms vs. dads and fight to give every parent the same opportunities.

This #LaborDay, I am especially grateful to the workers in Indiana and across America who are putting everything on the line for fair pay and better treatment. This holiday is a time to honor workers, but also a chance to reaffirm our commitment to them. https://t.co/DmhUdVVnpc
